problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 2x\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u⊥v$ and $x<0$, find the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
We know that $u⊥v$ ($u$ and $v$ are perpendicular) if and only if $u\cdot v=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y} \\  & =9\cdot (-2)+2x\cdot x \\  & =-18+2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ -18+2{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2} & =18 \\ {x}^{2} & =9 \\ x & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the positive solution since we are told that $x<0.$ Therefore, $x=-3.$
